realtime_controllers.peakshelf_note: With Peak/Shelf selected as a filter the FilFreq will sweep the 'MORPH' value between the two frames. So if you have a Morph = 0, FilFreq = 0 will represent the left frame, and FilFreq = 127 will represent the right frame.

shelf_semantics.quote: For a low pass filter, 'FREQ' defines the low pass rolloff, for mid shelf it defines the band, and for high pass it defines the highpass boundary. It acts as a controller for the filter type.
shelf_semantics.law: SHELF runs -64 (low-pass) through 0 (mid/peak) to +63 (high-pass); FREQ's meaning follows the shelf position.

display_conversion_code.fil_freq: int fil_freq (int input, int maxfreq, int mul) { int f = maxfreq; input = 255 - input; while (input-- > 0) f *= mul, f /= 1024; return f; } /* example fil_freq (100, 20000, 1002), in=0..255 */
display_conversion_code.cnv_morph_freq: void cnv_morph_freq (int input, char *buf) { sprintf (buf, "%dHz", fil_freq (input, 10000, 1006)); /*1009*/ } /* in=0..255 */
display_conversion_code.cnv_morph_gain: void cnv_morph_gain (int input, char *buf) { int gain10x = -240 + ((input * 120) / 32); ... } /* in=0..127 out=-24..+24 (32in ==> 12out) */

filter_tables.params: conversion bounds referenced for Peak dB and frame Freq

display_conversion_code.note: Frequency mapping is geometric (repeated multiply by mul/1024) — i.e. LOG-spaced steps, consistent with the packed runtime's log-morph behavior.
